subject: Pilot Commercials: batching/kv-cache credit structure and quantization risk-sharing
body:
From: Alex Chen <alex@finora.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify pilot economics + technical scope for batching/cache/quantize

Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Procurement asked me to get crisp commercial bullets for the pilot so we can move to a short SOW and a security review. Two quick asks from our side:

1) Can you outline the credit/discount structure if we enable KV-prefix caching and aggressive batching during the 6-week pilot?
2) What guardrails do you recommend around int4 quantization for our customer-facing models — we need a sense of risk/rollback and whether Redwood will credit us for measurable quality regressions.

Happy to share expected QPS and token mix if that helps.

—Alex
Head of AI Products, Finora

---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@finora.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify pilot economics + technical scope for batching/cache/quantize

Alex — good questions. Below is a concise commercial + technical proposal we discussed internally. Attaching a one-page commercial term sheet (optimize_proposal_v2.pdf) and a technical matrix (pilot_performance_matrix.xlsx).

Commercial summary (pilot 6 weeks):
- Pilot credits: 150,000 generation tokens + 50,000 embedding units included at no charge.
- If production rollout occurs within 90 days, credits convert and we offer a 12% post-pilot onboarding discount on list for first 6 months (subject to 12-month minimum commit).
- KV-prefix cache rebate: where prefix hits reduce billed generation tokens by up to 40% for cached prefixes (applied retroactively for the pilot period).
- Batching uplift: we estimate 18–28% token-cost reduction at your median sequence length if we keep a 30–50ms batching window. We will provide weekly batch-efficiency reports.
- Quantization concession: for an agreed test set, if int4 quantization results in >3% lower BLEU/ROUGE (model-specific metric) vs baseline, Redwood will credit the incremental token spend equivalent to 2 weeks of pilot usage.

Technical & risk mitigations:
- We recommend starting with int8+adaptive-KV quantization for production canaries, then trial int4 for read-only routes (non-monetized embeddings) for 2 weeks.
- Auto-rollback policy: if quality regressions exceed the threshold on the evaluation harness we’ll automatically route traffic to the int8 variant and re-run quantization tuning.
- Cache eviction: TTL 24 hours by default; we can open a MVL (manual validation loop) for prefixes with hallucination risk.

Next steps we propose:
1) Finora provides WIP token mix and a 3-day sample traces dump (we’ll sign an upload NDA).
2) Redwood delivers a customized pilot SOW + performance SLA and Docusign link.
3) Procurement and Security to review attached doc redline.

I’ve cc'd Karthik for the quantization specifics and Grace for commercial ops.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call Thursday if you want to walk line items.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@finora.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify pilot economics + technical scope for batching/cache/quantize

Alex — quick technical notes to flesh out Monica’s summary:

- Int4 guidance: For transformer decoders with long KV usage (avg context > 1k tokens), int4 can introduce distributional shifts in very long-range dependencies. Our recommended pattern:
  * Start with post-training static quantization to int8 and evaluate per-layer sensitivity.
  * Use block-wise mixed precision for attention layers (keep critical attention matmul in fp16).
  * Only enable int4 for the non-attention FFN layers initially; measure logits delta on your eval set.

- Quality detection: we’ll instrument a lightweight eval hook (sampled responses at ~0.5% of traffic) and compute custom metrics you provide plus perplexity delta. If delta > 3% on agreed metrics we flag and auto-roll to int8.

- Batching: with your traffic profile (burst QPS during business hours) we expect the 30–50ms window to hit most short-context requests into 8–16 request batches. That gives the 18–28% token-cost saving Monica referenced. We will publish the batch-size distribution after ingesting the trace.

- Billing nuance: cache-hit rebates apply only to exact-prefix matches. Approximate or fuzzy cache hits still bill but at a reduced multiplier (0.6x) because of reconstruction cost.

Happy to run a short guardrail test on your dev traces once we have the dump.

—Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex@finora.ai>

Cc: Finora Procurement <procure@finora.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify pilot economics + technical scope for batching/cache/quantize

Thanks — that is helpful. Procurement attached a redline (redline_finora_SOW_v1.docx) with two asks: 1) Can the post-pilot discount be guaranteed in the SOW (Procurement wants a written 12% for first 6 months after production conversion), and 2) limit the pilot liability to 30 days of equivalent credits rather than open-ended quality credits.

One more question from our infra team: when you say "apply rebate retroactively," does that mean we’ll receive a single credit line item on the final pilot invoice, or will you apply it weekly during the pilot?

We can share traces by end of day Friday if Redwood's legal and infra are ok with the upload process.

—Alex

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@finora.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Finora Procurement <procure@finora.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify pilot economics + technical scope for batching/cache/quantize

Alex / Procurement — understood. Proposed responses:

1) We can include the 12% onboarding discount in the SOW, conditional on passing the security review and signing the 12-month minimum commit within 90 days of pilot end. We will add precise language to the SOW to avoid ambiguity.

2) Liability cap: we accept Procurement's 30-day credit-cap for quantization-related regressions, provided Finora agrees on the evaluation harness and metric definitions before int4 trials begin. We’ll define "credit" as a dollar-equivalent token credit at your pilot rate.

3) Rebate cadence: we will apply cache-hit rebates weekly during the pilot as line-item credits in your weekly usage report; a final reconciliation will appear on the pilot close invoice.

If that sounds acceptable I’ll ask Legal to incorporate these points into the attached SOW redline and send a Docusign link for signatures. If Procurement wants different wording I can take your redline and produce a counter-redline by EOD tomorrow.

I’m available for a 30-minute call Friday 9am PT to finalize.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
